review.summary: Round 4 reviews the whole TASK-069A branch at the round-3 fix commit. All twelve round-3 findings are verified fixed, following the developer's instructions for client hard deletion once unreferenced, the narrowed review_stale claim with per-target value checksums, the last-used update on authorize and consistent New (ADR-015) markers with the relabelled apply step, and the recommendations for the rest: an ordered apply with pre-execution rejections that never write failed, the ARCHITECTURE.md summary, informational validate flags, foreign-key-enforcing cleanup tests, copied client_id with bounded client names and aligned log fields, the second-redemption wording, the review-read timeout and missing targets, and the TASK-069A $ref summary. Scope is still documentation-only. likec4@1.60.0 validate passes and the committed PNGs are byte-identical to a fresh export with the README command; all seven views were inspected; all 27 model elements have one tag; 76 relative links and anchors resolve. Seven new findings, all low or info: errors in apply's first three steps not classified, client growth bounded only by registration rate with last-used updated before validation, client name format characters and missing names, a broken ADR list, leftover client_id and timeout wording, UI tasks missing the self-declared label and missing-target display, and migration coverage of the change set's set-null rule.

findings.summary: Errors in apply's first three steps are not classified, so a lock-wait or recomputation timeout could still write failed.
findings.rationale: ADR-015 says only failures in re-validation, execution and commit mark failed, but TASK-069I, AI.md and the concept say a statement timeout marks failed without limiting it to those steps. The timeout now also covers the fingerprint recomputation and lock waits on the change-set row, so an apply that times out waiting for the lock after another apply ended review_stale could make a never-executed change set permanently failed.
findings.recommendation: State in all four places that any error in the lock, status check or recomputation, including a statement timeout, rolls back without writing failed and returns a retryable error, limit timeout to execution, and add a TASK-069I test for a timeout during recomputation.

findings.summary: Client rows are bounded only by the registration rate, and failing authorize calls can keep clients alive.
findings.rationale: A new client is kept for at least 30 days, registration is in the higher rate tier, and authorize updates the last-used time before validating the redirect URI, scope and resource, so periodic failing authorize calls keep registered clients alive indefinitely. Speculatively, a concurrent cleanup could hard-delete a client between authorize's client check and its insert and hit the restricting foreign key.
findings.recommendation: Reword the ADR claim to growth bounded by the registration rate over the 30-day window, update the last-used time only after authorize has validated and stored the pending request, conditionally on the client not being soft-deleted, and optionally add a configurable total-client cap.

findings.summary: Client name rules do not reject Unicode format characters, and a missing client name is unspecified.
findings.rationale: Only control characters and line breaks are rejected, so bidirectional overrides and zero-width characters could spoof or reorder the name and its self-declared label on the consent page. RFC 7591 makes the name optional, but the 1-to-100-character rule implicitly rejects a missing name and the column nullability is open.
findings.recommendation: Reject Unicode format characters as well as control characters, render the name isolated in TASK-069L, state whether a missing name is rejected or defaulted with a matching non-null column, and have TASK-069O confirm the real clients send one.

findings.summary: The ADR-015 registration rules have a broken list structure.
findings.rationale: The redirect URI allowlist sentence continues the last metadata-bounds sub-item, so the URI matching bullets render as siblings of the metadata bounds.
findings.recommendation: End the bounds sub-list and put the allowlist sentence back as its own paragraph under Registration.

findings.summary: Some summaries still omit the copied client_id, the review-read timeout or the refined client cleanup criterion.
findings.rationale: The DATA-MODEL.md change-set row, ADR-015's change-set introduction and TASK-069O's cleanup check list creator and client name without client_id; TASK-069I's limits bullet sets the timeout only for dry-run and apply; and TASK-069D describes client cleanup as clients without grants for 30 days instead of no active grant and last use older than 30 days.
findings.recommendation: Add client_id to those summaries, add the review read to TASK-069I's limits bullet, and align TASK-069D's cleanup wording.

findings.summary: The UI tasks do not require the self-declared label, client_id or a missing-target display.
findings.rationale: ADR-015 says the client name is always shown as a self-declared label and the review API reports deleted targets as missing, but TASK-069L's connections list and TASK-069M's review panel show the client without the label or client_id, and TASK-069M does not render missing targets.
findings.recommendation: Require the self-declared label and client_id in TASK-069L and TASK-069M, and a missing-target display with a Vitest case in TASK-069M.

findings.summary: With the SQLite option, the migration's set-null rule for the change set's grant reference is never tested.
findings.rationale: A SQLite run builds tables from the models, so it exercises the model's delete rule rather than migration 018, and TASK-069D's PostgreSQL test covers only the authorization request reference.
findings.recommendation: Have the migration 018 up and down PostgreSQL test also check the change set's grant reference becomes null, or require PostgreSQL for the cleanup test.

prior_finding_dispositions.rationale: ADR-015 now lists the apply steps in order with the fingerprint check before execution, states that a not-submitted 409 and review_stale never write failed and that only re-validation, execution and commit failures do, and AI.md, the concept lifecycle and TASK-069I agree; a remaining classification gap for errors in the first three steps is recorded as a new finding.

As the developer instructed, soft-deleted clients are hard-deleted once no authorization request or grant references them, with restricting client foreign keys, consistently in ADR-015, AI.md, DATA-MODEL.md and TASK-069D, E and F; a remaining growth and ordering issue is recorded as a new finding.

As instructed, the claim now covers changes to the flagged summaries, each flagged summary carries a per-target SHA-256 value checksum included in the fingerprint, the remaining in-transaction window is explicitly accepted, and TASK-069I adds a single-value-edit test.
ARCHITECTURE.md now summarises recomputed flags with per-target checksums and the 409 review_stale failure, matching ADR-015.
TASK-069J now returns the replacement computation from validate for information only, never stores it, and states that review and apply recompute it.

The TASK-069F and TASK-069I cleanup tests must run on PostgreSQL or on SQLite with foreign-key enforcement, following the existing customer model test pattern; a migration coverage gap is recorded as a new finding.

Change sets copy client_id as a plain value, client_name is bounded and sanitised and always labelled self-declared, and the revocation log fields are aligned between ADR-015 and TASK-069F; leftover summaries are recorded as a new finding.
As instructed, authorize now updates the client's last-used time, with a TASK-069E test that a client starting a consent flow is not cleaned up before the code exchange.
ADR-015 now distinguishes a second redemption after only the grant is gone (already consumed, nothing to revoke) from one after the request row is gone (unknown code).
The statement timeout now covers the review detail recomputation, and a target deleted after submit is reported as missing rather than raising, in ADR-015, TASK-069I and TASK-069K.

As instructed, every existing LikeC4 element that describes planned behaviour uses New (ADR-015), the generate flow apply step includes the fingerprint check, and all seven views were re-exported and match a fresh export byte for byte.
TASK-069A's decision summary now limits $ref to server-generated keys and uses client keys verbatim.
